guide_enrichment.narrative: We are not reacting to Missouri’s 54-14 opener as if one result settles this matchup. Austin Simmons was excellent in his debut, completing 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, and the defense held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 yards. That performance showed Missouri’s upside, but the market is asking for that dominance to translate into another substantial margin against a different opponent.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Troy’s passing offense against Missouri’s rebuilt defense. Our efficiency numbers strongly favor Missouri when Troy throws and when it tries to create scoring opportunities. The concern is clear: if Troy cannot sustain drives, Missouri will have repeated chances to create separation. Still, Missouri returned only two defensive starters from last season, so we are not treating one strong opener as complete confirmation that the new unit should be priced like the established 2025 defense. Our position rests on the market pushing the expected margin slightly further than our longer-run numbers support, even with Missouri owning the matchup advantages.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 home victory over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri scored 40 first-half points against Arkansas-Pine Bluff and outgained UAPB 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri finished the UAPB game with 562 total yards, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while allowing 198 total yards.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone opportunities against UAPB.
Missouri's defense forced five three-and-outs against UAPB.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is listed as Missouri's starting quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers as the backup.
Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in his Missouri debut against UAPB.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in his Missouri debut.
Simmons is the seventh different starting quarterback of the Eli Drinkwitz era and the third transfer quarterback to start for Drinkwitz at Missouri.
Zollers completed 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards and scored his first collegiate rushing touchdown in the opener.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed starting offensive line is left tackle Cayden Green, left guard Tristan Wilson, center Dominick Giudice, right guard Curtis Peagler and right tackle Luke Work.
Green, Giudice and Peagler returned as offensive-line starters from the 2025 team, while center Connor Tollison and tackle Keagan Trost were lost from last season's starting group.
Missouri lists Jamal Roberts as its starting running back, followed by Xai'Shaun Edwards or Malae Fonoti.
Roberts rushed 13 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the opener and surpassed 1,000 career rushing yards.
Sophomore receiver Donovan Olugbode set career highs with seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns against UAPB.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee caught five passes for 89 yards against UAPB, including a 47-yard touchdown from former Ole Miss teammate Austin Simmons.
Shaun Terry II recorded his first career touchdown reception in the opener.
Missouri lists Brett Norfleet or Jordon Harris at starting tight end.
Missouri lost starting quarterback Beau Pribula and starting receivers Kevin Coleman Jr., Marquis Johnson and Joshua Manning from the 2025 offense.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned only two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10 starters from that unit.
Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez and safety Santana Banner ranked second and third on Missouri in tackles in 2025; Rodriguez had three starts and Banner had one start that season.
Defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb combined for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025, with Webb recording 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith recorded 4.0 sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025 and is listed as Missouri's starting JACK defender in 2026.
Auburn transfer Robert Woodyard Jr. is listed as Missouri's starting middle linebacker after making 11 starts and recording 67 tackles for Auburn in 2025.
Ole Miss transfer Chris Graves Jr. is listed as a starting cornerback after playing in 41 games and making nine starts for Ole Miss in 2025.
Elijah Dotson recorded his first collegiate tackle for loss and forced fumble against UAPB, while Jason Dowell recorded his first collegiate sack.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 after previous coordinator roles at Michigan, North Carolina, Auburn, Arizona State, UCF and Southern Miss; he was Troy's head coach from 2019-21.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating special teams at Florida State.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri as tight ends coach in January 2026 after coaching tight ends and coordinating the run game at LSU in 2025.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator to his linebackers-coach title before the 2026 season.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, ranking eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri produced a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances in 2025.
Missouri rushed for 31 touchdowns in 2025 and scored three rushing touchdowns in the 2026 opener.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, including 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri allowed 198 yards, 14 points and a 23% third-down conversion rate in its 2026 opener.
Missouri did not force a turnover against UAPB but held the Golden Lions to 89 rushing yards and 109 passing yards.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is listed as Missouri's placekicker, Brunno Reus as its punter and kickoff specialist, Brett Le Blanc as its long snapper and DaMarion Fowlkes as its primary returner.
Craig made a 32-yard field goal and all seven extra-point attempts against UAPB.
Fowlkes recorded a 23-yard punt return and Reus had a 52-yard punt in the opener.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri has won 15 consecutive regular-season nonconference games dating to Sept. 17, 2022.
Missouri has won 24 consecutive home games against non-SEC opponents dating to Oct. 21, 2017.
Missouri has won 12 consecutive home night games and 14 consecutive regular-season night games.
Missouri's Sept. 19 game against Troy is scheduled for 6 p.m. CT at Faurot Field.
